Franco Volpi, an Italian philosopher, wrote Nihilism as a history of one of philosophy's darkest concepts. He develops an earlier synopsis of the problem into a full account, following nihilism from its roots in German idealism onward.

The story runs through Nietzsche, who named nihilism as Europe's coming crisis, and into the twentieth century, where the collapse of old values became a central theme of thought. Volpi writes as a historian of ideas, tracing who used the word and what each meant by it. The book suits readers of continental philosophy who want the concept's whole career.
